rows.en: Yet the man himself had no interest whatsoever in such fame,
and he would end up wandering space alone. But that is another story.
Meanwhile, though the Macross 7 fleet had lost Battle 7,
it journeyed on through space, once again in search of a new planet to settle.
Searching for a place, somewhere out there, to call home for good...
rows.notes: Fragment after a full stop, as in the Japanese ('seeking a place of permanent settlement somewhere...').

rows.en: The giant Ranka was an illusion draped over
the Battle Galaxy, which had been placed under Grace's control.
Ranka, who had been held captive inside the Galaxy,
regained consciousness thanks to Sheryl's song and Alto's voice.
But now it was Sheryl, her strength spent, who collapsed.
Alto and Ranka called out to Sheryl, trying to rouse her.
And then, a miracle happened.
Recognized by the Vajra through Ranka, Sheryl
was at last freed from the grip of the V-type virus.
Sheryl and Ranka sang, each striving to outdo the other.
Their song gave strength to a renewed counterattack against Grace.
What's more, the power of Ranka and Sheryl's songs
even freed the Vajra that Grace had held under her control.
The Vajra and humanity formed a united front and stood against Grace.
Faced with that power, Grace was no longer any match for them.
Grace's ambition to rule the galaxy by exploiting both the Vajra and humanity
was thus shattered.
Their battle over, the Frontier fleet set down on the Vajra homeworld.
Humanity and the Vajra: utterly different life-forms that never got along.
And yet it turned out they could understand one another.
And so a new world was born, where the Vajra and humanity live side by side...
Revived after absorbing Sara, the Bird Human used its overwhelming might
to wreak utter destruction, bent on wiping out a humanity that kept fighting.
In that hopeless situation, Shin's voice managed to awaken Sara's heart.
But Operation Iconoclasm had already been set in motion.
Reaction weapons flew to destroy the Bird Human, deemed uncontrollable.
To protect Earth, Mayan Island, and above all Shin, Sara flew off into space,
taking with her the reaction weapons she had sealed away with her own power.
Thus both ruin by the Bird Human and reaction-weapon fallout were averted.
But Shin's fighter had lost all control and was simply plummeting.
His ejection system had failed too, leaving him no way to escape.
Shin's fighter, which seemed certain to crash,
began to climb, wrapped in a mysterious light,
as the people of Mayan Island looked on,
rows.notes: Mid-sentence: Shin's fighter began to climb ... as the people of Mayan Island watched ... as if chasing Sara.

rows.en: as if chasing after Sara, who had vanished into space...
Before the enemy's overwhelming strength, the Macross seemed helpless.
But then, an unexpected ally appeared.
Moved by Minmay's song, Vrlitwhai and a faction of the Zentradi forces
had risen in revolt against Boddole Zer.
Refusing to let humanity be wiped out and its Culture lost,
rows.notes: TM had lowercase 'culture'; glossary term is 'Culture'.

rows.en: Vrlitwhai's forces covered the Macross as it drove on through space.
Along the way, it cut down Zentradi soldiers left bewildered by Minmay's song.
At last, the Macross closed in on the heart of the Main Fleet,
Boddole Zer's mobile fortress.
The only way for humanity to survive was to destroy the enemy's nerve center.
As the Macross launched its attack,
the Valkyries stormed into the mobile fortress.
The Main Fleet's commander and core unit of Boddole Zer's mobile fortress,
Golg Boddole Zer, was destroyed.
With its chain of command gone, the Main Fleet
no longer had the strength to attack the Macross.
And so the Space War, fierce beyond measure, came to an end.
Leaving behind the legend of Minmay's song...
The Galaxy Whale was struck by the poachers' reaction weapon.
But the whale shrugged off the reaction weapon as if it were nothing.
Seeing this, Basara began singing to the whale.
And then something unexpected happened.
The Galaxy Whale responded to Basara's song and let out a cry.
Or rather, it began singing along with Basara's song.
Singing together with Basara, the Galaxy Whale
absorbed tremendous energy and shook the ground of Zola.
It held a power that overwhelmed all who witnessed it.
Eventually the whales vanished into the far reaches of the galaxy, still singing.
And so the session that seemed like it might never end
between Basara and the whales came to a close.
Thanks to the efforts of the Zolan Star Patrol, the poachers were swept away.
Satisfied after singing his heart out with the whales, Basara
left Zola behind and flew off to the far reaches of space.
Under a sudden Vajra attack, the Galaxy fleet sent out a distress signal.
But the Frontier government ignored the distress signal.
rows.notes: Frontier seifu = the Frontier government (glossary has only the 'Administrative Bureau' form, needs_research).

rows.en: Told by Grace that the Galaxy fleet was in danger, Sheryl
paid S.M.S. out of her own pocket to go to the Galaxy fleet's rescue.
rows.notes: Japanese: with her own pocket money she requested S.M.S. to rescue the Galaxy fleet. 'paid ... to go to the rescue' carries both.

rows.en: Taking the job, S.M.S. launched Mission "Galactic Fairy."
rows.notes: Japanese: 'In response to this request, mission "Galactic Fairy" was launched.' Made S.M.S. the subject of the active verb; mission name from lore 'Galactic Fairy' (episode/mission title not in glossary missions).

rows.en: In the cockpit of Alto's fighter, bound for the battlefield, Sheryl's earring glittered.
Meanwhile, on Island 1, Sheryl's revenge concert had begun.
rows.notes: 'revenge live' = Sheryl's revenge concert (the rematch of her interrupted concert).

uncertain: u4145: mission name rendered Mission "Galactic Fairy" from the lore term; terms.json missions has no entry for it.
u4073/u4074 (TM kept): English order puts 'under Grace's control' on the second row, whereas the Japanese has it on the first; left as is because re-cutting reads badly.
